verdict.rationale: The DGX B300 is on-premises hardware that customers install and run themselves. The docs cover fit in MGX and traditional enterprise racks, AC/PDU and DC/busbar power options, N+N redundant PSUs, BMC/Redfish/IPMI remote management, on-site RAM upgrades, and a self-installable DGX OS (Ubuntu) with RHEL/Rocky support. A community comment corroborates that running your own B300 server is far cheaper, though it notes very high power demands. Missing for 10: detailed site-preparation and installation documentation, and hands-on corroboration of a self-hosted deployment.
